title: Enforcement Rule of the Youth Welfare Support Act
full_text:
ENFORCEMENT RULE OF THE YOUTH WELFARE SUPPORT ACT

Article 1 (Purpose)
This Rule prescribes matters delegated by the Youth Welfare Support Act and its Enforcement Decree and matters necessary for their enforcement.

Article 1-2 (Subjects of Fact-finding Surveys)
(1) Fact-finding surveys on youth in crisis under Article 2-2(1) of the Youth Welfare Support Act (hereinafter the "Act"; hereinafter a "fact-finding survey") shall cover: <Amended 2023.6.28; 2025.10.1>
1. General characteristics, including sex and age;
2. Family and living environments;
3. Experiences of crisis;
4. Psychological and emotional conditions;
5. Safety and welfare;
6. Other matters the Minister of Gender Equality and Family considers necessary as basic data for policies to improve youth welfare.
(2) Surveys shall use sampling and may employ interviews, questionnaires, online surveys, or other methods.
(3) Where necessary for efficient implementation, the Minister may commission a youth-policy research institution (including a school under Article 2 of the Higher Education Act), corporation, organization, or other entity to conduct a survey. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(4) The Minister shall publish survey results under Article 2-2(1) of the Act on the website of the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family. <Amended 2023.6.28; 2025.10.1>
(5) The Minister shall determine detailed procedures, methods, and other necessary matters beyond paragraphs (1) through (4). <Amended 2025.10.1>

Article 2 (Applications for Youth Cards)
(1) A youth applying under Article 4(1) of the Act shall submit an application for issuance in attached Form No. 1 with one photograph to a Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu (the head of a Gu means the head of an autonomous Gu; hereinafter the same applies), regardless of address. <Amended 2014.12.30; 2019.8.2; 2023.6.28>
(2) If the applicant requests a certificate confirming the application for temporary identification before the card is issued, the authority receiving the application under paragraph (1) shall receive one additional photograph and issue the certificate in attached Form No. 2. <Amended 2019.8.2>
(3) Any of the following may apply on the youth's behalf for issuance or reissuance under paragraph (1) or Article 4: <Amended 2023.11.22>
1. A legal representative, including a person with parental authority;
2. A person actually protecting the youth at a youth facility under Article 3, subparagraph 6 of the Framework Act on Youth;
3. A person actually protecting the youth at a child welfare facility under Article 52(1) of the Child Welfare Act.

Article 3 (Issuance of Youth Cards)
A Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu receiving an application under Article 2(1) shall verify the applicant or representative, enter the relevant particulars in the youth card issuance register in attached Form No. 3, and issue the card. <Amended 2014.12.30; 2019.8.2>

Article 4 (Loss of Youth Cards)
(1) If a card is lost or damaged, its holder may apply for reissuance to a Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu regardless of address, using attached Form No. 1 with the youth card attached (only if damaged). <Amended 2014.12.30; 2019.8.2>
(2) A holder wishing to change the recorded particulars shall apply to the above authority regardless of address, using attached Form No. 1 with the card and documents proving the changes attached. <Amended 2014.12.30; 2019.8.2>
(3) The authority receiving an application under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall verify the applicant or representative, enter the particulars in the register in attached Form No. 3, and issue the card. <Amended 2014.12.30; 2019.8.2>
(4) If an applicant has not collected a card within six months after applying outside the jurisdiction of the applicant's address, the authority issuing and holding it shall send it to the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over that address. <Amended 2019.8.2>

Article 5 (Destruction of Youth Cards)
The issuing authority shall destroy a youth card (in subparagraph 1, the damaged card) upon either of the following: <Amended 2019.8.2>
1. An application for another card due to damage;
2. The passage of one year after a collection notice concerning a card held due to loss or other reasons or issued under Article 3 or 4.

Article 6 (Youth Cards)
(1) A card under Article 4(1) of the Act shall conform to attached Form No. 4.
(2) When issuing a card under paragraph (1), printing the impression of the official seal (the shape produced by stamping it) may replace affixing the seal. <Amended 2019.8.28>

Article 7 (Physical Fitness Tests and Health Examinations)
(1) Physical fitness tests and health examinations under Article 6(1) of the Act (hereinafter "health examinations, etc.") shall prioritize youth aged nine through 18 among out-of-school youth under Article 2 of the Act on Support for Out-of-School Youth (hereinafter "out-of-school youth"). <Amended 2015.5.29>
(2) They shall follow youth health and physical fitness standards under Article 3 of the Enforcement Decree of the Youth Welfare Support Act (hereinafter the "Decree") and examination items and methods under Article 25(5) of the Enforcement Decree of the National Health Insurance Act. <Amended 2015.12.31; 2019.8.2>
(3) The Minister of Gender Equality and Family, a Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Metropolitan City Mayor, Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Do Governor, or Special Self-Governing Province Governor (hereinafter a "Mayor/Do Governor"), and the head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall announce a detailed implementation plan, including the period and place, when conducting health examinations, etc. <Amended 2019.8.2; 2025.10.1>
(4) A youth, the youth's guardian, or a youth leader under Article 3(7) of the Framework Act on Youth (hereinafter a "youth leader") shall submit attached Form No. 5, an application for a youth physical fitness test and health examination, with proof of out-of-school status (only for out-of-school youth), to the Minister, a Mayor/Do Governor, and the head of a Si/Gun/Gu. A guardian or youth leader applying shall obtain the youth's consent. <Amended 2019.8.2; 2025.10.1>
(5) On receiving attached Form No. 5 under paragraph (4), the Minister, a Mayor/Do Governor, and the head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall verify the following documents through joint use of administrative information under Article 36(1) of the Electronic Government Act. If the youth or guardian does not consent, submission of the documents shall be required. <Amended 2015.5.29; 2025.10.1>
1. Deleted <2019.8.2>
2. A certified copy of the resident registration record.
(6) On receiving the application under paragraph (4), the above authorities shall decide whether to conduct health examinations, etc. within 30 days after application and notify the applicant. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(7) They shall notify the youth of the results within 30 days after the examinations, etc. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(8) They shall take appropriate measures for a youth found to require disease treatment or other measures. <Amended 2025.10.1>

Article 7-2 (Applications for Menstrual Hygiene Products)
(1) A person applying under Article 5(3) of the Act and Article 3-2 of the Decree shall submit an application for support for female youths' menstrual hygiene products in attached Form No. 5-2 with a copy of identification to a Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu. A representative shall additionally attach proof of representative status. <Amended 2019.8.2; 2022.4.21>
(2) The receiving authority may verify eligibility documents, including a recipient certificate, second-lowest-income confirmation, or single-parent family certificate, through joint use of administrative information under Article 36(1) of the Electronic Government Act. If the applicant does not consent, the applicant shall submit the documents directly. <Amended 2019.8.2; 2022.4.21>
(3) The receiving authority shall decide whether to provide support within 14 days after receipt and notify the applicant using the approval or rejection notice in attached Form No. 5-3. <Amended 2019.8.2; 2022.4.21>
(4) Notwithstanding paragraphs (1) and (3), applications or approval/rejection notices made using the social security information system under Article 37(2) of the Framework Act on Social Security may follow common forms determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Health and Welfare under Article 13 of the Enforcement Rule of the Act on the Use and Provision of Social Security Benefits and Search for Eligible Beneficiaries. <Amended 2022.4.21>

Article 7-3 (Staffing of Dedicated Integrated Support System Organizations)
(1) Dedicated public officials assigned under Article 9-2(2) of the Act shall have any of these qualifications:
1. Qualification as a youth instructor under Article 21 or youth counselor under Article 22 of the Framework Act on Youth;
2. At least two years' experience in youth-development duties under Article 3, subparagraph 2 of that Act;
3. Recognition by the local government head as qualified for the post, as prescribed by local ordinance.
(2) Private-sector specialists assigned under Article 9-2(2) of the Act shall have any of these qualifications:
1. Qualification as a youth counselor under Article 22 of the Framework Act on Youth;
2. A bachelor's degree or higher in counseling and welfare;
3. Recognition by the local government head, as prescribed by local ordinance, as having knowledge and practical experience in youth counseling and welfare.
(3) The head and working-level personnel of the dedicated organization may be assigned as dedicated public officials under Article 9-2(2) of the Act.

Article 8 (Scope of Families Below a Specified Income)
"Specified income prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family" in Article 13(3) of the Act means 60 percent of standard median income under Article 2, subparagraph 11 of the National Basic Living Security Act. <Amended 2015.12.31; 2025.10.1>

Article 9 Deleted <2015.12.31>

Article 10 (Applications for Special Support for Youth in Crisis)
(1) An applicant under Article 15(1) of the Act shall apply to a Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu using the common form (application for social welfare services and benefits) determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Health and Welfare for social welfare programs and services under Article 42 of the Enforcement Rule of the National Basic Living Security Act. <Amended 2019.8.2>
(2) The receiving authority shall verify the documents below by the specified methods: <Amended 2015.12.31; 2019.8.2; 2023.4.11>
1. Proof of eligibility for selection under Article 8 of the Decree (documents including certified copies or extracts of resident registration records or computerized family relationship registration information): Verification through joint use of administrative information under Article 36(1) of the Electronic Government Act (hereinafter "joint use of administrative information"). However, proof shall be required to be submitted in either of these cases:
(a) The applicant (including household members; hereinafter the same applies in this paragraph) does not consent to that verification;
(b) The responsible official cannot verify eligibility by that method.
2. Income and asset declaration under Article 35(1)4 of the Enforcement Rule of the National Basic Living Security Act: Verification through use, under Article 37(6) of the Framework Act on Social Security, of the social security information system under paragraph (2) of that Article (hereinafter the "social security information system"). However, documents verifying the youth's household income and assets shall be required in any of these cases:
(a) The applicant does not consent to verification through that system;
(b) The responsible official cannot verify the household's income and assets through it;
(c) The applicant's entries in the common form under paragraph (1) differ from the information in that system.
3. Deleted <2015.12.31>

Article 11 (Management of Special Support for Youth in Crisis)
For youth currently receiving or having received special support, a Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall prepare and manage a special-support management card using the common form determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Health and Welfare under Article 42 of the Enforcement Rule of the National Basic Living Security Act for social welfare programs and services. <Amended 2019.8.2>

Article 11-2 (Educational Support for Youth Parents)
"Matters prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family" in Article 18-4(1)4 of the Act means support for care of the children being raised by youth parents during their period of study. <Amended 2025.10.1>

Article 12 (Applications for Protective Support)
An applicant for preventive and restorative protective support under Article 19(1) of the Act (hereinafter "protective support") shall submit the application in attached Form No. 6 to a Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu.

Article 13 (Selection Procedures for Recipients of Protective Support)
(1) The authority receiving an application under Article 12 shall conduct a basic investigation and counseling; if protective support is considered necessary, it shall conduct a professional investigation and counseling and, after deliberation by the committee under Article 10 of the Act, decide whether to provide support, its content and duration, and other matters within 30 days after application. If special circumstances exist for investigation and counseling, it may extend the period by up to 14 days. <Amended 2019.8.2; 2021.9.24>
(2) The basic investigation and counseling shall cover:
1. Whether delinquency or deviant behavior exists and its particulars;
2. The youth's living environment, including home and school;
3. Other matters necessary to decide whether guidance is needed.
(3) Professional investigation and counseling shall cover:
1. The youth's personality and aptitude;
2. The youth's aspirations, studies, and career path;
3. Other matters necessary to determine the direction and duration of guidance.

Article 14 (Decisions on Protective Support)
When deciding to provide protective support, a Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall separately notify the youth, guardian, and school head in writing of the gist of the decision, support content and duration, and other matters. If the youth or guardian applied, the school head shall be notified only with the youth's or guardian's consent. <Amended 2019.8.2>

Article 15 (Duties of Protective Support Guardians)
(1) A protective support guardian under Article 21(1) of the Act shall perform these duties: <Amended 2019.8.2>
1. Counseling and support for the youth;
2. Submission of opinions on changes to support content and termination or extension of the support period;
3. Other advice for the youth's healthy growth.
(2) A Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu may pay guardians allowances and necessary activity expenses within budget limits. <Amended 2019.8.2>

Article 16 (Reports on Establishment of Youth Welfare Facilities)
(1) Under Article 32(2) of the Act, a person other than the State or a local government intending to establish a facility under Article 32(1) of the Act (hereinafter a "youth welfare facility") shall submit a report in attached Form No. 7 (an electronic report may replace it), with the following documents attached (electronic documents may replace them), to a Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu: <Amended 2019.8.2>
1. Articles of incorporation (only for a corporation);
2. A list of assets needed for operation (with proof of ownership or right of use; verification by the receiving authority through joint use of administrative information under Article 36(1) of the Electronic Government Act may replace that proof);
3. A business plan and budget;
4. A floor plan showing area by floor and structural section, and a building layout plan (only if the plans cannot be verified from the building register under paragraph (2));
5. A personnel list and copies of qualification certificates (only for personnel requiring such certificates).
(2) The receiving authority shall verify corporate registration (only for a corporation), building and land registration certificates, and the building register through joint use of administrative information under Article 36(1) of the Electronic Government Act, and issue a facility report certificate in attached Form No. 8. <Amended 2019.8.2>

Article 16-2 (Protection upon Compulsory Discharge from Youth Shelters)
(1) Under Article 32-2(2) of the Act, a youth shelter operator shall, before discharging an out-of-home youth, request consultation with the head of a relevant institution, such as a youth welfare facility under Article 31 of the Act (hereinafter in this Article a "relevant institution"), so that the youth can receive protection and support, including admission, from it.
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), if the discharged youth does not wish to receive protection and support such as admission to a relevant institution, the operator shall provide follow-up care, including information on protection and support services, for at least six months after discharge.

Article 17 (Reports on Suspension or Closure)
(1) A person intending to suspend or close a facility or resume operation under Article 33 of the Act shall submit the report in attached Form No. 9, with the following documents, to the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of a Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over its location, at least one month before suspension (closure or resumption): <Amended 2019.8.2>
1. A statement of reasons [for a corporation, a copy of board-meeting minutes resolving on suspension (closure or resumption)];
2. A plan for measures for youth using the facility (hereinafter "facility users"), except on resumption;
3. The facility report certificate (only on closure).
(2) On receiving the report, the authority shall take any of these measures to protect facility users' rights and interests: <Amended 2019.8.2>
1. Verify implementation of the plan under paragraph (1)2;
2. If subsidies, donations, or donated goods were received, verify their actual use;
3. Other measures necessary to protect facility users' rights and interests.

Article 18 (Qualifications and Staffing Standards)
(1) Qualification standards by occupation for facility personnel under Article 34(3) of the Act are set out in attached Table 1; staffing standards by occupation are set out in attached Table 2.
(2) Facility personnel may receive training to improve their capabilities in youth protection and support under Article 34(2) of the Act.

Article 19 (Standards for Administrative Dispositions)
Standards by type of violation under Article 35(2) of the Act are set out in attached Table 3.

Article 20 (Identification of Inspecting Public Officials)
Identification under Article 39(2) of the Act shall conform to attached Form No. 10.

Article 21 (Evaluation Criteria and Methods)
(1) Performance evaluation criteria for youth welfare support institutions, youth welfare facilities, or institutions or organizations entrusted with youth welfare duties under this Act, pursuant to Article 41(1) of the Act, are:
1. Appropriateness of the institution's or facility's environment;
2. Appropriateness of its operation and personnel management;
3. Appropriateness of program content;
4. Service satisfaction of users and residents.
(2) The Minister of Gender Equality and Family shall evaluate performance of those institutions, facilities, or entrusted institutions or organizations under Article 41(2) of the Act every three years. <Amended 2025.10.1>

Article 22 (Standards and Methods for Entrusted Operation)
(1) When entrusting operation under Article 42-2(1) of the Act to a youth organization (excluding an organization established by the State or a local government to operate the institution or facility), the State or local government shall select the person entrusted with operation (hereinafter the "entrusted operator") through open recruitment, comprehensively considering financial capacity, public credibility, program-delivery capability, and other factors.
(2) A committee for deliberating selection of entrusted operators (hereinafter the "selection committee") shall be established within the State or local government intending to establish the facility (hereinafter the "entrusting authority") to deliberate on selection under paragraph (1).
(3) The committee shall comprise no more than nine members, including one chairperson. The head of the entrusting authority shall appoint or commission members from among the following and designate its chairperson from among its members:
1. Public officials responsible for youth welfare;
2. Persons with extensive learning and experience in youth welfare;
3. Persons recommended by public-interest organizations;
4. Other persons, including legal experts, whose participation the head considers necessary.
(4) A meeting opens with a majority of incumbent members present and passes resolutions by a majority of those present.
(5) Other operational matters shall be determined by the head of the entrusting authority after committee deliberation.

Article 23 (Entrustment Contract Contents)
(1) A contract with a youth organization selected under Article 22(1) shall include:
1. The entrusted operator's name and address;
2. The contract term;
3. Entrusted facilities and duties;
4. The operator's obligations and matters to observe;
5. Safety management of youth welfare support institutions and facilities;
6. Succession to employment of their personnel;
7. Contract termination;
8. Other matters deemed necessary for operating the institutions and facilities.
(2) The contract term under paragraph (1)2 shall not exceed five years. If necessary, the entrusting authority may extend it by up to five years following selection committee deliberation. <Amended 2021.9.24>

Article 24 Deleted <2016.12.27>

Qualifications for Personnel of Youth Welfare Facilities (related to Article 18(1))

ENFORCEMENT RULE OF THE YOUTH WELFARE SUPPORT ACT [Attached Table 1] <Amended 2025.10.1>
QUALIFICATIONS FOR YOUTH WELFARE FACILITY PERSONNEL (Article 18(1))
(a) Youth Shelters and Youth Self-reliance Support Centers
Occupation | Qualification standards
Head:
1) Doctorate or completion of a doctoral course in counseling/welfare, plus at least three years' practical experience at youth welfare facilities, including experience before the degree.
2) Master's degree in counseling/welfare, plus at least five years' such facility experience, including experience before the degree.
3) Professional qualification for youth protection/support, such as youth counselor, youth instructor, social worker, clinical psychologist, or family counseling specialist, plus at least five years' practical youth counseling/welfare experience.
4) At least five years' practical youth counseling/welfare experience, recommendation by a specialized institution or organization as possessing ability and aptitude for youth protection/support, and recognition by the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of Si/Gun/Gu.
Protection/counseling staff and self-reliance support staff:
1) Graduation from a four-year or longer university course in counseling/welfare or equivalent or higher education recognized by another statute.
2) Graduation from a four-year or longer university course or equivalent or higher education recognized by another statute, plus at least two years' practical youth counseling/welfare experience.
3) Junior college graduation in counseling/welfare or equivalent or higher education recognized by another statute, plus at least two years' such experience.
4) Graduation in a counseling/welfare-related department at a special-purpose high school under Article 90 of the Enforcement Decree of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act (hereinafter a "special-purpose high school") or specialized high school under Article 91 of that Decree (hereinafter a "specialized high school"), or equivalent education recognized under another statute, plus at least four years' practical youth counseling/welfare experience (including experience before graduation or recognition of education).
5) Professional qualification for youth protection/support, such as youth counselor, youth instructor, social worker, clinical psychologist, or family counseling specialist.
6) Qualification as a vocational skills development training teacher under the Workers Vocational Skills Development Act.
7) Recognition as having qualifications equivalent to items 1) through 6).
Administrative staff:
1) High school graduation or higher and recognition as capable of the duties.
2) Recognition as having equivalent qualifications.
Cook:
Cook qualification or at least two years' cooking experience, and capability to perform the duties.
Notes:
1. "Counseling/welfare field" means counseling, education, psychology, social welfare (social work), youth (guidance) studies, and fields recognized as related to counseling/welfare by a Mayor/Do Governor or head of Si/Gun/Gu.
2. "Practical youth counseling/welfare experience" means either of the following, including experience before obtaining the qualification or degree:
(a) Full-time counseling/welfare work for youth at youth-related institutions or organizations;
(b) Full-time youth-policy work in youth-related fields of the State or a local government.

(b) Youth Treatment and Rehabilitation Centers
Head:
1) Doctorate or completion of a doctoral course in a youth treatment/rehabilitation-related field, plus at least five years' practical experience in such a field.
2) Master's degree in such a field, plus at least seven years' such experience.
3) Professional qualification as a psychiatrist, youth counselor, youth instructor, social worker, or clinical psychologist, plus at least seven years' relevant practical experience (including before qualification).
4) State or local government public official of Grade 4 or higher with at least five years' practical experience in youth treatment/rehabilitation-related fields.
5) At least 10 years' such experience, recommendation by a specialized institution or organization as possessing ability and aptitude for youth protection/support, and recognition by the Minister of Gender Equality and Family or local government head.
Management supervisor:
1) Doctorate or completion of a doctoral course in a youth treatment/rehabilitation-related field, plus at least three years' practical experience in such a field.
2) Master's degree in such a field, plus at least five years' such experience.
3) Professional qualification as a psychiatrist, youth counselor, youth instructor, social worker, or clinical psychologist, plus at least five years' relevant practical experience (including before qualification).
4) State or local government public official of Grade 5 or higher with at least five years' such experience.
5) Regular teacher qualification under Article 21(2) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, plus at least five years' practical experience in medicine, psychology, counseling, welfare, or youth-related work (including before qualification).
6) At least seven years' youth-related practical experience, recommendation by a specialized institution or organization as possessing ability and aptitude for youth protection/support, and recognition by the Minister of Gender Equality and Family or local government head.
Counselor:
1) Junior college graduation in counseling, education, or psychology, or equivalent or higher education recognized by another statute, plus at least two years' relevant practical experience (including before the degree).
2) Youth counselor or professional school counselor qualification under Article 21 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act.
Protection/self-reliance support staff:
1) Professional youth instructor or social worker qualification.
2) Junior college graduation in youth (guidance) studies, social welfare (social work), or education, or equivalent or higher education recognized by another statute, plus at least two years' relevant practical experience (including before the degree).
3) Graduation in a department related to youth studies, youth guidance, social welfare, social work, or education at a special-purpose or specialized high school, or equivalent education recognized by another statute, plus at least four years' relevant practical experience (including before graduation or educational recognition).
Doctor:
Psychiatrist qualification under Article 77 of the Medical Service Act.
Nurse:
1) Mental-health nurse qualification under Article 17 of the Act on the Improvement of Mental Health and the Support for Welfare Services for Mental Patients, plus at least one year's relevant practical experience (including before qualification).
2) Nurse license under Article 7 of the Medical Service Act, plus at least one year's relevant practical experience (including before qualification).
Therapist/clinical psychologist:
1) Junior college graduation in psychotherapy or clinical psychology, or equivalent or higher education recognized by another statute, plus at least one year's relevant practical experience (including before the degree).
2) Mental-health clinical psychologist qualification under Article 17 of the Act on the Improvement of Mental Health and the Support for Welfare Services for Mental Patients, plus at least one year's relevant practical experience (including before qualification).
3) Accredited qualification in psychotherapy, cognitive therapy, or special therapy under Article 23 of the Framework Act on Qualifications, plus at least two years' relevant practical experience (including before qualification).
Administrative staff:
1) High school graduation or higher and recognition as capable of the duties.
2) Recognition as having equivalent qualifications.
IT staff:
Industrial engineer qualification or higher in computing under the National Technical Qualifications Act, plus at least three years' experience in related fields (information systems, networks, and office computing equipment), including before qualification.
Dietitian:
Dietitian license under Article 15 of the National Nutrition Management Act.
Cook:
Cook license under Article 53 of the Food Sanitation Act or at least two years' cooking experience, and recognition as capable of the duties.
Facility manager:
License or qualification in facility management, such as architecture, electricity, machinery, firefighting systems, building services, industrial safety, piping, or heat management.
Driver:
Class 1 ordinary driver's license or higher, plus at least three years' driving experience at State institutions, local governments, public institutions, or similar entities.
Notes:
1. "Youth treatment/rehabilitation-related fields" means youth (guidance) studies, child studies, counseling, education, psychology, social welfare (social work), sociology, medicine, and nursing.
2. Relevant practical experience means the following, including experience before obtaining the qualification or degree:
(a) Full-time counseling/welfare and education/activity/guidance work for youth in nonprofit institutions or organizations related to youth, society, or culture;
(b) Full-time youth-policy work in youth-related fields of the State or a local government;
(c) Full-time medical care or counseling work for youth at medical institutions or youth-related institutions/organizations.

(c) Youth Recovery Support Facilities
Head:
1) Doctorate in counseling/welfare or juvenile protection.
2) Completion of a doctoral course in either field, plus at least three years' practical youth counseling/welfare or juvenile-protection experience.
3) Master's degree in either field, plus at least five years' such experience.
4) Qualification as a youth counselor, youth instructor, social worker, elementary school teacher, secondary school teacher, kindergarten teacher, childcare teacher, or a professional youth protection/support qualification such as family counseling specialist, plus at least five years' practical youth counseling/welfare or juvenile-protection experience.
5) At least five years' such experience, recommendation by a specialized institution or organization as possessing ability and aptitude for youth protection/support, and recognition by the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or head of Si/Gun/Gu.
Protection/counseling staff:
1) Graduation from a four-year or longer university course in counseling/welfare or juvenile protection, or equivalent or higher education recognized by another statute.
2) Graduation from a four-year or longer university course or equivalent or higher education recognized by another statute, plus at least two years' practical youth counseling/welfare or juvenile-protection experience.
3) Junior college graduation in counseling/welfare or equivalent or higher education recognized by another statute, plus at least two years' practical youth counseling/welfare experience.
4) Graduation in a counseling/welfare-related department at a special-purpose or specialized high school, or equivalent education recognized by another statute, plus at least four years' practical youth counseling/welfare experience (including before graduation or educational recognition).
5) Qualification as a youth counselor, youth instructor, social worker, elementary school teacher, secondary school teacher, kindergarten teacher, childcare teacher, or a professional youth protection/support qualification such as family counseling specialist.
6) Recognition as possessing qualifications equivalent to items 1) through 5).
Notes:
1. "Counseling/welfare field" means counseling, education, psychology, social welfare (social work), child welfare (child welfare services), youth (guidance) studies, and related fields recognized by a Mayor/Do Governor or head of Si/Gun/Gu.
2. "Juvenile protection field" means correctional protection studies, police administration, law, criminal sociology, correctional studies, and related fields recognized by a Mayor/Do Governor or head of Si/Gun/Gu.
3. "Practical youth counseling/welfare experience" means either of the following, including experience before obtaining the qualification or degree:
(a) Full-time counseling/welfare work for youth at youth-related institutions or organizations;
(b) Full-time youth-policy work in youth-related fields of the State or a local government.
4. "Practical juvenile-protection experience" means any of the following, including experience before obtaining the qualification or degree:
(a) Full-time juvenile-protection work for juveniles at juvenile-protection institutions or organizations;
(b) Full-time juvenile-protection policy work in juvenile-related fields of the State or a local government;
(c) Service as an entrusted protective-custody member commissioned under Article 33(1) of the Juvenile Trial Rules.

STANDARDS FOR ADMINISTRATIVE DISPOSITIONS AGAINST YOUTH WELFARE FACILITIES (Article 19)
1. General Standards
(a) Standards based on violation frequency apply where an administrative disposition for the same violation was imposed within the preceding year. The period is calculated from the date of that disposition to the date the same violation is detected after it.
(b) When aggravating under item (a), use the stage immediately following that of the preceding disposition (the highest stage if two or more dispositions occurred within that period).
(c) If two or more violations attract different dispositions, apply the heavier standard. If two or more are business suspensions, the heavier suspension may be increased by up to one-half, but cannot exceed the sum of applicable periods or one year.
(d) On transfer or inheritance of a facility or corporate merger, the transferee, heir, or surviving corporation succeeds to the effects of dispositions imposed before the transfer, inheritance, or merger, including dispositions whose period has expired and those still running.
(e) The authority may mitigate a disposition considering motivation, particulars, gravity, and the following. Business suspension may be reduced by up to one-half of the standard period; replacement of the head may be reduced to 15 days' suspension; closure may be reduced to replacement of the head:
1) The violation results from minor carelessness or error, rather than intent or gross negligence;
2) Its particulars and gravity are minor and harm to victims and others is considered small;
3) No suitable alternative protective facility is available for residents if business is suspended.
